A fair 2026 comparison of 11x and AiSDR across pricing, channels, setup, and track record, with published numbers and attributed facts. Jaspar Carmichael-Jack 8 minutes read · Jul 27, 2026 Key Takeaways AiSDR publishes its pricing openly: roughly $250, $900, and $2,500/month across its tiers, per its pricing page. 11x now publishes a Growth tier from $3,750/month billed annually (about $45K/year), with Pro and Enterprise tiers still custom. 11x has raised roughly $74M from investors including a16z and Benchmark. It runs Alice for multichannel outreach and Julian, a named AI phone agent. AiSDR centers on email and outbound plus inbound, with "Ami," a strategist agent, and a fast, self-serve setup. Its center of gravity is small and midsize business (SMB) and lower mid-market buyers. 11x drew documented scrutiny in 2025: TechCrunch reported customer claims the company could not support (March 24, 2025), its founder-CEO stepped down to non-executive chairman in May 2025, and chief technology officer Prabhav Jain became CEO. Reviewers report deliverability and CRM-sync complaints against 11x. AiSDR's constraint is a thinner enterprise governance story rather than reported reliability issues. Choose AiSDR for transparent pricing and speed to launch; choose 11x if a voice channel and enterprise-style onboarding are the priority. 11x and AiSDR are both AI SDR tools, software that stands in for a sales development representative (SDR) and runs outbound prospecting for you, but they sell and price very differently. AiSDR publishes flat monthly tiers from $250 and sets up fast, which suits smaller teams. 11x runs multichannel outreach plus an AI phone agent through enterprise-style annual contracts, and carries more baggage from 2025. If you want a quick read, AiSDR is the more transparent, lower-commitment starting point, and 11x is the pick when a named AI phone agent and a guided enterprise-style rollout matter more than self-serve pricing.
